headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend intact, long-term trend still repairing

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The uptrend is intact, so the current posture supports increasing acquisition budget, with emphasis on active-trader channels that tend to respond most in this phase. Confidence is medium rather than high because the longer-term trend is still recovering and price is well below its previous peak, so a staged increase fits better than a single large one. This is budget-posture guidance based on trailing data, not trading advice.

reasons: Price is 18% above its 200-day average; 90-day gain is about 40%.
Weekly RSI near 60 shows firm momentum without overbought conditions.
The 200-day average is still falling (-5.3% over 90 days), limiting conviction.
Price is 33% below its all-time high; Fear & Greed is 73 (Greed).
watch: The main tension is between fast recent gains and a slow long-term trend: price is up about 40% in 90 days, yet the 200-day average is still falling and only 47% of recent days closed above it. With the 10-year yield at 5.24% and markets focused on inflation data, a slip below the 200-day average would weaken the read, while a flattening 200-day slope and broader participation would strengthen it. These are trailing measures, not forecasts.
analysis: Short-term mood is warm but not stretched: Fear & Greed reads 73 (Greed), funding is only mildly positive (z +0.44) and longs outnumber shorts 1.42 to 1 on about $2.4B of open interest, so leverage looks measured. Implied volatility is subdued (DVOL 35.8, VIX 16.1) even as BTC eased to roughly $83K on the day; CoinDesk attributes the pullback to rising Treasury yields and oil, with markets positioning ahead of Wednesday's PCE inflation print.

Momentum remains the strongest leg of the read. BTC is up about 40% over 90 days, weekly RSI of 59.8 is firm without being overbought, and the 50-day average sits roughly 8% above the 200-day. Participation is thinner than the headline gain implies, with only 47% of recent days closing above the 200-day average, and spot ETF inflows cooled to about $31M on the latest day. On the calendar, the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets has a comment deadline of 20 October, and the next FOMC meeting is 27 October.

On the long view, price sits 18% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.18) and 1.27x its 200-week average, but the 200-day line is still sloping down (-5.3% over 90 days) and price is 33% below its all-time high, which reads more like a recovery than a mature bull phase. Macro is mixed: the 10-year yield at 5.24% is well above the 3.63% fed funds rate. Against that, cumulative ETF inflows near $57.6B and about 1.28M BTC held by public companies point to sustained institutional holding.
